subject: Chemistry
description: Hydrocarbons advanced — alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, isomers, aromatics (benzene), petrochemicals, fractional distillation, cracking.

questions.explanation: ALKANES — saturated hydrocarbons; only single C−C bonds; general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. EXAMPLES: methane CH₄ (n=1), ethane C₂H₆ (n=2), propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀, pentane C₅H₁₂, hexane C₆H₁₄, heptane C₇H₁₆, octane C₈H₁₈, nonane C₉H₂₀, decane C₁₀H₂₂. PROPERTIES: chemically INERT (saturated bonds), low reactivity except combustion + halogenation. STATES at room T: C₁-C₄ gas (methane, ethane, propane, butane); C₅-C₁₇ liquid (gasoline, kerosene, diesel range); C₁₈+ solid (waxes, asphalt). HYDROCARBON GENERAL FORMULAS: (1) ALKANES: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (saturated). (2) ALKENES: CₙH₂ₙ (one C=C double bond). (3) ALKYNES: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (one C≡C triple bond). (4) CYCLOALKANES: CₙH₂ₙ (ring, single bonds). (5) AROMATIC: typically based on benzene C₆H₆. INDIA INDUSTRIAL: NATURAL GAS (mostly CH₄) increasingly used for cooking (PNG/CNG); LPG = liquefied propane + butane (used in household cylinders). CALORIFIC VALUE — alkanes are excellent fuels: methane ~55 MJ/kg, octane ~47 MJ/kg, ethanol (not alkane but for comparison) ~30 MJ/kg. NOMENCLATURE: IUPAC system uses prefix-suffix to count carbons + indicate type. PYQ FREQUENCY: alkane formula in NEET, NCERT, JEE-Main 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: BENZENE has the structure of a:

options.option_text: Six-membered aromatic ring with delocalized π electrons
Linear chain of six carbons (option here) too

questions.explanation: BENZENE (C₆H₆) — flat, hexagonal ring of 6 carbon atoms; each C has 1 H attached. AROMATIC because: (1) Cyclic. (2) Planar. (3) All atoms in ring sp²-hybridized. (4) Has 6 π-electrons in delocalized π-orbitals (Hückel's 4n+2 rule, n=1). RESONANCE: alternating single-double bonds in two structures average to ALL EQUIVALENT bonds (~139 pm, between single 154 pm and double 134 pm). HISTORICAL: F.A. KEKULÉ (1865, Germany) proposed cyclic structure after a dream of a snake biting its own tail (legend). KEKULÉ STRUCTURES: alternating C=C bonds (Lewis structure approximation). MODERN: delocalized π electrons (more accurate). PROPERTIES: clear, COLORLESS LIQUID, BP 80°C; sweet aromatic smell; CARCINOGEN (causes leukemia); flammable. USES: solvent, raw material for plastics (polystyrene, polyester), nylon (caprolactam intermediate), drugs. AROMATIC COMPOUNDS: benzene + derivatives (toluene, xylene, naphthalene, anthracene). KEKULÉ-NAMED rings + 1,3,5-cyclohexatriene = benzene. POLYAROMATIC HYDROCARBONS (PAHs): naphthalene (mothballs), anthracene; in coal tar, vehicle exhaust — many carcinogenic. PYQ FREQUENCY: benzene structure in NEET, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: ACETYLENE (used in welding torches) has the chemical formula:
questions.explanation: ACETYLENE — IUPAC name ETHYNE — chemical formula C₂H₂; the SIMPLEST ALKYNE (contains C≡C TRIPLE BOND). STRUCTURE: H−C≡C−H (linear); strong triple bond stores high energy. PROPERTIES: colorless gas, distinctive garlic-like smell (impurity), explosive at high pressure (>2 atm), highly flammable. PRODUCTION: industrially from CALCIUM CARBIDE + WATER → CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂↑. COMMERCIAL: stored DISSOLVED in acetone in cylinders (avoids explosive pressure). USES: (1) OXY-ACETYLENE TORCH — welding/cutting metals (flame ~3000°C, hottest commercial flame). (2) Production of vinyl chloride (PVC plastic precursor), acrylonitrile (polymers). (3) FRUIT RIPENING — calcium carbide releases acetylene which mimics ethylene plant hormone (BANNED in India under FSSA — health hazard for fruit ripening; modern method uses ETHYLENE). (4) Old GAS LAMPS (carbide lamps) for caves, bicycles, miners. (5) Rocket propellant in some applications. RELATED: ETHYLENE C₂H₄ (ALKENE) — used to ripen fruits naturally; raw material for polyethylene plastic. METHANE CH₄ — natural gas, simplest alkane. PYQ FREQUENCY: acetylene formula and uses in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: FRACTIONAL DISTILLATION is used to separate:
questions.explanation: FRACTIONAL DISTILLATION — crude oil (PETROLEUM) is heated in REFINERY column; different hydrocarbon fractions VAPORIZE and CONDENSE at different heights based on their BOILING POINTS. KEY FRACTIONS (top to bottom of column, low to high BP): (1) PETROLEUM GAS (LPG) — methane, ethane, propane, butane (BP < 40°C). (2) PETROL/GASOLINE — C₅-C₁₂ (40-180°C). (3) NAPHTHA — C₆-C₁₀, raw material for petrochemicals. (4) KEROSENE — C₁₀-C₁₆ (180-260°C); aircraft fuel (jet fuel). (5) DIESEL — C₁₂-C₂₀ (~260-340°C); trucks, generators, ships. (6) FUEL OIL — heavy fraction, ships, industrial heating. (7) LUBRICATING OIL — engine oil, grease. (8) PARAFFIN WAX — candles, polishes. (9) BITUMEN/ASPHALT — road surfaces, roofing. INDIA REFINERY CAPACITY: ~5 million barrels/day (4th largest globally). KEY REFINERIES: Reliance Jamnagar (largest in world, 1.24 million b/d), IOC Mathura, BPCL Mumbai. CRACKING: heavier fractions broken down to lighter, more valuable ones using catalysts (FCC — Fluid Catalytic Cracking). REFORMING: low-octane to high-octane gasoline. INDIA crude imports: ~85% imported (from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, UAE, Russia). PYQ FREQUENCY: fractional distillation in NEET, NCERT 1× per cycle.

options.option_text: Only one form of butane only

questions.explanation: BUTANE C₄H₁₀ has TWO STRUCTURAL ISOMERS: (1) n-BUTANE (normal butane) — straight chain: CH₃−CH₂−CH₂−CH₃. (2) ISO-BUTANE (or 2-methylpropane) — branched: (CH₃)₃CH = CH₃−CH(CH₃)−CH₃. BOTH have formula C₄H₁₀, same molecular weight, but DIFFERENT physical/chemical properties. KEY DIFFERENCES: (a) BP: n-butane −0.5°C; iso-butane −12°C (branched is slightly more compact, weaker van der Waals → lower BP). (b) Density, solubility differ slightly. NUMBER OF ALKANE ISOMERS by C count: 1 (CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ all have only 1); 2 (butane); 3 (pentane); 5 (hexane); 9 (heptane); 18 (octane); 35 (nonane); 75 (decane). RAPID GROWTH: more carbons → exponentially more isomers. PROPANE C₃H₈: only ONE structure (CH₃−CH₂−CH₃; branching impossible). LPG: COMMERCIAL LPG = ~60% n-butane + ~40% propane (varies by season). 'I-BUTANE' / 'ISOBUTANE' is also a refrigerant (R-600a, used in modern eco-friendly fridges). USES of BUTANE: (1) LIGHTER fluid. (2) AEROSOL propellant. (3) Refrigerant. STRUCTURAL ISOMERISM: same formula, different connectivity. Other types: STEREOISOMERISM (same connectivity, different spatial arrangement). PYQ FREQUENCY: alkane isomers in NEET, JEE-Main 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: ETHENE (ethylene) is used in industry as the basis for which polymer?
questions.explanation: ETHENE / ETHYLENE C₂H₄ — simplest alkene; polymerizes to POLYETHYLENE (PE), the world's MOST PRODUCED PLASTIC (~100 million tonnes/year globally). REACTION: n × CH₂=CH₂ → −(CH₂−CH₂)−ₙ (polymerization with catalysts like Ziegler-Natta). TYPES OF POLYETHYLENE: (1) LDPE (Low-Density) — flexible, used for plastic bags, films, squeeze bottles. (2) HDPE (High-Density) — stiff, used for milk jugs, containers, water pipes. (3) LLDPE (Linear LDPE) — combines properties. USES: plastic bags, bottles, pipes, electrical insulation, packaging films, geomembranes. ETHYLENE — also used as: (1) PLANT HORMONE — naturally produced by ripening fruits; ripens others (banana with apple = banana ripens fast). (2) PRECURSOR for ETHYLENE GLYCOL (antifreeze, polyester PET fabric). (3) ETHANOL production. (4) Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) — via vinyl chloride. (5) Polystyrene — via styrene. INDIA: Reliance, IOC, GAIL, ONGC operate large ethylene crackers. PROBLEM — PLASTIC POLLUTION: PE is SLOWLY DEGRADING (centuries); ocean garbage patches; bans on single-use plastics. SOLUTIONS: recycling (limited), bioplastics (PLA), reduce-reuse-recycle. INDIA banned single-use plastic items (1 July 2022). PYQ FREQUENCY: PE-ethylene link in NEET, NCERT, JEE-Main 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: OCTANE NUMBER of a fuel measures:
questions.explanation: OCTANE NUMBER (or 'octane rating') — measures a fuel's ability to RESIST 'KNOCKING' (premature ignition) in spark-ignition engines. Higher octane = better resistance = smoother engine performance, especially in high-compression engines. SCALE: (1) ISO-OCTANE (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) = 100 (very resistant). (2) n-HEPTANE = 0 (highly knock-prone). FUEL OCTANE NUMBER = % of iso-octane in a hypothetical iso-octane/n-heptane blend with same knocking. INDIA PETROL OCTANE: regular petrol is 91 RON (Research Octane Number); premium 'Speed Plus' / 'XTRA Premium' is 95-99 RON. RACING fuels: 100+ RON. KNOCKING (PINGING): when fuel ignites BEFORE the spark reaches it (due to compression heat) → 'pinging' sound, engine damage. HIGH-COMPRESSION ENGINES (e.g., turbocharged) need HIGHER octane. ADDITIVES historically used: TETRAETHYL LEAD ((C₂H₅)₄Pb) — banned globally due to LEAD POISONING (health, environment). Replacement: ETHANOL (10-20% blend in petrol — also boosts octane); MTBE (in some countries, but contaminates groundwater). E20 INITIATIVE in INDIA (2025): 20% ethanol blend in petrol — reduces import + emissions. CETANE NUMBER — analogous for DIESEL fuels (measures ignition quality, not anti-knock). PYQ FREQUENCY: octane number in NEET, JEE-Main, GA 1× per cycle.
